question: What will the Arctic sea ice extent be on October 11, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Arctic sea ice extent for 2026-10-11 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I could read the official NSIDC daily file only through **2026-08-26**, when extent was **4.983 million km²**. That is about 0.08 above the same day in 2025. Over 2018-2025, October 11 values ranged from 4.96 to 6.13. Many search results were published after 2026-09-06; I left them out as instructed.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 daily CSV. The newest row I could read was 2026-08-26: 4.983 million km². I could not get rows from Aug 27 to Sep 6; the copy I fetched ended there. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- August 2026 daily values from the CSV: Aug 1: 6.495; Aug 10: 5.896; Aug 15: 5.354; a brief rise to 5.414 on Aug 18; Aug 21: 5.265; Aug 25: 4.998; Aug 26: 4.983. [NSIDC CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv)
- Earlier 2026 milestones from the same file: Mar 13 peak 14.358 (5-day maximum 14.29 on Mar 15), Jul 1: 9.034, Jul 31: about 6.53. [akclimate](https://akclimate.org/arctic-sea-ice-extent-july-31-2026/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Extent was near its seasonal minimum as of early September, and the October 11 value depends on when the minimum comes and how fast the ice refreezes afterwards.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-03: NSIDC put the August 2026 average at 5.56 million km², 7th lowest on record and 840,000 km² above 2012. Ice tracked 2012 levels until August. There was a lot of open water in the Beaufort, Chukchi and East Siberian Seas, and much of the Beaufort had melted out by month's end. A persistent low over the pole kept the summer cool and cloudy, with May-July temperatures at 925 hPa up to 2°C below average. Melt onset in the Chukchi was late. [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses/arctic-zigs-antarctic-zags)
- Early Sep 2026: Copernicus said August 2026 extent was about 9% below the 1991-2020 average, 12th lowest for August. [Copernicus](https://climate.copernicus.eu/sea-ice-cover-august-2026)
- 2026-08: The Met Office reported extent of 7.02 million km² on Aug 2 (9th lowest for the date) and called the September outcome highly uncertain. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)

## 4. Base rates (NSIDC v4 daily CSV, million km²)

| Year | Aug 26 | Sep 6 | Sep min (date) | Oct 1 | Oct 11 | Gain, Aug 26 to Oct 11 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 5.095 | 4.874 | 4.630 (Sep 21) | 5.054 | 5.300 | +0.21 |
| 2019 | 4.636 | 4.371 | 4.166 (Sep 18) | 4.828 | 5.069 | +0.43 |
| 2020 | 4.429 | 3.899 | 3.793 (Sep 13) | 4.497 | 4.963 | +0.53 |
| 2021 | 5.303 | 4.897 | 4.757 (Sep 14) | 5.395 | 6.132 | +0.83 |
| 2022 | 5.287 | 4.866 | about 4.69 (mid-Sep) | 5.319 | 5.935 | +0.65 |
| 2023 | 4.739 | 4.428 | 4.244 (Sep 17) | 4.755 | 5.599 | +0.86 |
| 2024 | 4.547 | 4.289 | 4.245 (Sep 10) | 4.720 | 5.171 | +0.62 |
| 2025 | 4.904 | 4.664 | 4.543 (Sep 8) | 5.260 | 5.868 | +0.96 |
| 2026 | 4.983 | not retrieved | | | | |

- October 11 values in 2018-2025 averaged about 5.50, with a range of 4.96 to 6.13.
- The gain from Aug 26 to Oct 11 ranged from +0.21 to +0.96, averaging about +0.64. The spread (about 0.75) is wide, and it depends mostly on how fast the ice refreezes in early October.
- In 2025, extent rose almost 0.6 in ten days, from 5.260 on Oct 1 to 5.868 on Oct 11. Day-to-day jumps of 0.1-0.2 are common in October.
- Of these years, 2026 on Aug 26 was closest to 2025 (4.904), 2018 (5.095) and 2023 (4.739).
- I did not get pre-2018 values; 2012's record low would be an outlier on the low side.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket ran a market on the minimum Arctic extent this summer, resolving on NSIDC daily data for Aug 1 to Oct 1, 2026. I could not see its prices; the aggregator page returned a 403 error. [frenzycap](https://www.frenzycap.com/predictions/event/polymarket/min-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer)
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold market, and no expert forecast specifically for October 11 extent.
- In July, the Met Office said a September extent within the post-2007 range was highly likely. [Met Office August briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The minimum itself: historically between about Sep 8 and Sep 21. Its timing and depth set the starting point for refreeze.
- The pace of refreeze from late September to early October: the persistent low and the cool central Arctic NSIDC described could speed it up. The open Beaufort, Chukchi, East Siberian and Laptev/Kara sectors refreeze at different rates.
- NSIDC's minimum announcement (mid to late September) and its early-October monthly analysis.
- Practical points: daily values are preliminary and can be revised slightly. The question uses the daily column, not the 5-day average NSIDC quotes in its announcements; these can differ by about 0.05-0.1.
